focus: Marvell buys Lumentum for $115B in stock (4.5 MRVL per LITE); MRVL -3.3%, LITE -5.8%
Oil slides on U.S.-Iran talk: WTI $99.36 (-4.6%), Brent $108.45 (-4.4%); XLE -1.3%
Chips bounce after Friday's rout (SMH -7.0%): SMH +1.0%, QQQ +0.6% premarket
Palantir (±13.2% priced) and Apple (±4.3%) report after the close
Oracle -3.8% on a $10B bond sale; CrowdStrike +2.6% on a Deutsche Bank upgrade
ISM manufacturing 10:00 ET; midterms tomorrow; AMD, SMCI, ANET report Tuesday
bigPicture: The market punishes debt-funded, cash-burning AI spenders (Oracle's bond sale, Alphabet and Amazon's negative free cash flow) and pays suppliers only when orders are confirmed.
October was the Nasdaq's worst month in over a year and Friday closed S&P -1.8%, Nasdaq -2.9%; today's bounce is a relief bid with no new AI earnings behind it yet.
With a Dec 9 hike the base case (~75-85% in futures) and the 10-year near 4.93%, high-multiple tech is the funding source whenever yields rise.
Oil is the swing factor: an Iran deal eases inflation and helps rate-sensitive tech, but U.S. reports say strikes are being prepared after the midterms.
snapshot.takeaway: A relief bounce with no new AI earnings behind it: the tests are Palantir and Apple tonight and AMD, SMCI and ANET tomorrow, with the midterms in between. Let the 10:00 ISM print and the first 15 minutes show whether buyers hold the premarket highs before trusting any long-side setup.
